This is in line with the findings reported here: https://forum.liquibase.org/topic/mysql-creating-boolean-columns-as-bit-1-instead-of-tinyint-1

My suggestion is to change all boolean types to `TINYINT(1)` in the Liquibase schema files.

What do you think. @dkayiwa ?
@WolfSchlegel do you foresee any side effects of the change to tinyint(1) for other databases like PostgreSQL?

Off-hand: `tinyint` is a MySQL-specific extension to the SQL standard. Postgres has a `smallint`, but it’s not exactly equivalent (it’s also part of the SQL standard). In any case, Postgres supports a native `boolean` type.

It’s kind of unfortunate that the Liquibase team chose to change the mapping. We might need to use a custom datatype to continue to support `tinyint(1)` and other databases (afaict, MySQL’s official line is still that `boolean` should map to `tinyint(1)`).

Thanks for suggesting a custom datatype, @ibacher , that got me thinking in a different direction.

Options I can see at this point include:

1. Accept BIT as a datatype for MySQL booleans as of `liquibase-schema-only-2.1.x.xml`.
   Pros: Nothing needs to be changed
   Cons: This option would deviate from MySQL's type system and it is unknown Hibernate would respond to that change. The latter is hard to test.

2. Hard-code TINYINT(1) in changelog files as of `liquibase-schema-only-2.1.x.xml`.
   Cons: This would couple the changelog files to MySQL (as @dkayiwa  pointed out earlier)
   Pros: The con is too overwhelming to consider any pros
   
3. Implement a custom datatype (as Ian suggested)
   c.f. https://www.liquibase.org/javadoc/index.html?liquibase/datatype/DataTypeFactory.html
   Pros: Uses a Liquibase mechanism 
   Cons: There do not seem to be custom datatypes in OpenMRS and there are not many examples availabe (which is a minor con)
   
4. Use a changelog parameter
   c.f. https://www.liquibase.org/documentation/changelog_parameters.html
   Pros: Uses a Liquibase mechanism and looks easier to implement than a custom datatype
   Cons: None I can see
   
I am going to try No. 4, please let me know how you assess the options and if there are more options.

Cheers,
Wolf
I like the simplest option that works with no cons. Just in case you were not aware of this: https://wiki.openmrs.org/display/docs/Liquibase+Extensions

Thanks @dkayiwa , that helps a lot. 

Option 4 is fighting back with an `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` raised by Liquibase which is not easy to understand so I switch horses and go for option 3 instead.

Mixed news, the good news are: 
- Got option 4 working, the exception was triggered by a typo.
- All automated tests pass.

The bad news are:
- The new property in the change log files interferes with Liquibase check sums, when restarting OpenMRS all changesets that use the new property are not recognised as "was run before" but re-applied:

etc.
etc.

Cheers,

@WolfSchlegel I think, quite intentionally, there is no way we can fix this without interfering with Liquibase checksums (that is what they're there for). The simple option is to add a `<validChecksum>` element at the top of the offending entry, e.g. `<validChecksum>8:238fe3f03c37d18fd5117d58579b728e</validChecksum>` will cause Liquibase to accept the old checksum as being correct for the new change (and not otherwise alter the checksum of the change).

Also, fwiw, I like the use of changelog parameters better than what I was suggesting. Not a feature I was aware of. Very cool!

@WolfSchlegel The content of the changeset will change inasmuch as the value is changing from "BOOLEAN" to "tinyint(1)", right? I'm under the impression that Liquibase checksums are generated from a normalised version of the command and not the underlying SQL, but I'd be happy to be contracted on that.

Hey there,

I hope you have a good weekend. I certainly had a productive Saturday as...

**tl;dr**

TINYINT(1) is back (yay!)

**The long version**

Where to start? I learned many things in the last 24 hours:

1. The ways to extend Liquibase changed over time, e.g. the class extended by the [`OpenmrsMySQLTypeConverter`](http://svn.openmrs.org/repo/openmrs-contrib/liquibase-ext/type-converter/trunk/src/java/liquibase/ext/OpenmrsMySQLTypeConverter.java) of old no longer exists in the current Liquibase release.

2. The current documentation of the Liquibase extension points is also stale, e.g. `liquibase.database.AbstractDatabase` described [here](https://liquibase.jira.com/wiki/spaces/CONTRIB/pages/2424845/Database) also no longer exists.

3. Still, that page got me started as it mentions how to register extensions with Liquibase (at the bottom of [this page](https://liquibase.jira.com/wiki/spaces/CONTRIB/pages/2424845/Database)). So I had a look at the [Liquibase Javadoc](https://www.liquibase.org/javadoc/index.html?index-all.html) pages.

4. The [index for the letter R](https://www.liquibase.org/javadoc/index-all.html#I:R) contains multiple entries for methods name `register(...)` and [this one](https://www.liquibase.org/javadoc/liquibase/datatype/DataTypeFactory.html#register-java.lang.Class-) caught my attention. Liquibase supports custom data types.

5. The next step was to implement a new class `MySQLBooleanType` that extends `liquibase.datatype.core.BooleanType` and returns `TINYINT(1)` as the appropriate data type for boolean fields when applying a changelog to a MySQL database (or MariaDB). For other databases the new class delegates back to its superclass.

6. The new approach passes all tests, no more checksum blues and the boolean fields in the generated tables are of type `TINYINT(1)`.
